Nature & food

species noun

also a species, species of animal, species of plant, kind of animal, endangered species

classical

Cic. N.D. 2.99: quam varia genera bēstiārum vel cicurum vel ferārum (Lewis & Short)
Quint. 5.10.21: piscium genera (Lewis & Short)

genus, generis n.

noun, third declension · Declension on Wiktionary

kind, species (of animals, plants)

The classical word for a kind of animal or plant: avium genera, omne genus ferārum. In modern taxonomy genus is the rank above the species (M-O s.v. species: genus), so in a scientific context use speciēs.

Other words

  • speciēs, speciēī f. — species (in taxonomy)

    noun, fifth declension · also used · modern · M-O s.v. species (plant or animal taxonomy), after Pallas (1811); Varr. RR 3.3.3: in bīnās speciēs dīvidī (Lewis & Short) · Declension on Wiktionary

    Classically a look, an appearance, and in logic a subdivision of a genus (Cic. de Or. 1.189, Sen. Ep. 58.7); the biological rank is modern. In Cicero’s day its genitive and dative plural were not used (Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • quae vērō et quam varia genera bēstiārum vel cicurum vel ferārum!

    and what kinds of beasts, tame and wild, and how varied!Cic. N.D. 2.99

See also animal, kind.
